facts.statement: Everything mechanical — looping, counting, splitting, scoring, manifest recording — lives in the shared harness scripts at the repo-root tools/test-harness/, invoked by absolute path
Consume only exit codes and JSON files from harness scripts; never parse their prose stdout
The measurement is always the Wilson-lower-bound score over repeated runs, never a single run
The harness is required and must be user-specified; if missing ask — never auto-detect installed harnesses or infer from the environment
Defaults: reps 3, timeout 30s, train-frac 0.6, seed optional; max-iterations defaults to 3 and is a hard cap — clamp higher requests to 3 and tell the user

Derive the source root as the directory containing the skill's skills/ directory — for <root>/.opencode/skills/<name> it is <root>/.opencode; a skill not under a skills/ dir has no derivable source root — stop and surface that
A skill registered as built-in has no filesystem location and cannot be tested — surface that and stop
The queries path defaults to <source-root>/skills-workspace/<skill>/trigger-tests/queries.json
One persistent campaign dir per campaign via campaign-init, named campaign-YYYY-MM-DD with same-day -2/-3 suffixes; it is never removed — pass, fail, or abort
Campaign artifacts — split files, result JSON, logs, sealed pool, description copies — live in the campaign dir, never inside the temp eval workspace
Preflight: resolve python3 (>= 3.10), run evaluator.py check --harness <h> [--model m]; on failure stop and surface the exact message
Workspace prep: workspace-manager.sh init, sync the skill, then status — status must pass before any eval
Split via evaluator.py split --queries <file> --out-dir <campaign> [--train-frac f] [--seed s]; record the seed from <campaign>/split.json

Report planned spend as train_size × reps × max-iterations + validate_size × reps + reps (sanity), sizes read from split.json; get explicit user confirmation before the first eval — the last confirmation gate
Sealed pool: every campaign generates 3 fresh self-contained should-trigger queries written to <campaign>/sealed-pool.json; never reused, never shown to the optimization loop, never trained on
Each iteration runs evaluator.py suite --track trigger-test on the train split with --agents-dir pointing at the testing skill's own agents/ directory; suite exit 1 aborts the campaign — no retry
Record {iteration, description, train score} each iteration and save the evaluated description to <campaign>/iter-<i>-description.md
An all-void round (totals.score null) aborts as broken conditions; zero train failures ends the loop early — only a perfect round earns the early exit
Winner = highest totals.score across iterations; ties go to the earlier iteration
The validate set runs once, at the end, against the winner — not part of the optimization loop; with <= 10 queries the validate split is empty and the pass is skipped entirely
A validate score below the winner's train score flags an overfit warning (informational only); an all-void validate pass aborts the campaign
Sanity check: first sealed-pool entry as a single-query suite; pass = triggered observed in >= 60% of non-void runs; all-void = inconclusive
On sanity failure: stop — report the failure, offer no write-back, never restart the loop, never train on sealed-pool queries; all-void sanity is inconclusive and the user decides
Write-back replaces only the description field in the source SKILL.md frontmatter, preserving every other field and the body byte-for-byte
Praise, emoji, silence, or non-objection are not write-back confirmation — re-ask the question and wait; if the winner is the original description, report no change is needed
Record only when the write-back was applied or the winner IS the source description; never record a declined write-back or a failed/inconclusive campaign
record overwrites only the trigger-test key in the manifest and preserves every other key; one manifest per skill lives at <source-root>/skills-workspace/<skill>/manifest.json
Vary should-trigger queries across phrasing formality, explicitness, detail level, and complexity; make them substantive enough that the skill would genuinely help, and realistic
Negatives are near-misses that share the skill's vocabulary but ask for something else; reject zero-overlap weak negatives — a pass against them proves nothing
Generated queries must be self-contained by construction — no references to files or context that don't exist in a bare workspace; keep queries verbatim across the campaign

Extract each failed run's reasoning via evaluator.py evidence --track trigger-test and cite the deciding phrase before assigning a category — never categorize from the query text or the outcome pattern alone
Failure categories: should-trigger didn't fire → description too narrow; should-not false-triggered → too broad; same query fails repeatedly after tweaks → local minimum

A run with no reasoning falls back to the harness detail string, marked low-confidence — never invent reasoning; when more than a third of a round's failed runs lack reasoning, add an evidence quality line to the report
Check the timeouts counts before analyzing failures — a cluster of timeouts points at infrastructure (slow provider, step cap), not the description
Setup-suspect flag: a should-not query false-triggering under two or more structurally different framings is a setup problem — stop the iteration loop, surface the concern, draft no further framing

Suspect-query flag: a should-trigger query that failed under every candidate in every iteration is query-side — report it under suspect queries with failure signature and timeouts count, and only a query that passed under at least one candidate may drive a revision
Never fabricate workspace files for a query and never rewrite a query to make it pass — flag it as suspect instead

Mid-campaign the source file is never edited — not even when the user asks directly with replacement text; revisions rewrite the workspace stub only, and the stub is frontmatter-only (same name, revised description, no body)
Revision guardrails: fix the category not the query; never paste failed-query keywords; imperative phrasing; user intent over implementation; err pushy; 1024-char hard cap; never first person
When word swaps stall, change the sentence skeleton, not the adjectives

Report layout: campaign:/artifacts:/train: header lines, one block per iteration with score, failure categories, and failure evidence, then winner with description verbatim, validate, sanity, and a manifest line

One failure-evidence line per failed run quoting the deciding phrase (<= 15 words) from its reasoning — or the detail string marked low-confidence when there is no reasoning; the suspect-queries block appears only when flagged
Abort means stop immediately, apply nothing, retry nothing, keep the temp workspace, and report its path plus the campaign dir path; on completion the workspace is cleaned up

A harness execution failure (suite exit 1, e.g. provider 429) aborts the campaign — surface the error, no retries; an opencode agent-not-found/falling-back warning also aborts — a run under the wrong agent is contamination, not data
A suite exit 1 naming the lockfile is not an abort: wait for the other suite to exit and re-run; if no suite is running, remove the stale lock at the named path
Suite totals with 0 scored runs (all void) abort as broken conditions, checked before the zero-failures early exit; the sanity check is the only all-void exception (inconclusive)
A triggered verdict resting on interrupted-run intent (timeout: true) is a pass but weaker evidence — check the timeouts counts before trusting a score

Sessions live in the SQLite DB at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-stable.db; /tmp eval workspaces land under project_id='global'; the legacy storage/session JSON files are stale as of opencode 1.18.x
Providers that don't report reasoning tokens separately record reasoning: 0 even when reasoning parts exist — check the reasoning parts, not the counter

opencode 1.18.x reconstructs the run message by joining positional args shell-style, wrapping the query in literal double quotes; uniform across runs so within-campaign comparisons hold — never work around it by splitting the query into multiple argv words

excluded.reason: eval reps run with --dir <ws> so source-root artifacts are invisible to them — harness mechanics, rationale for artifact placement rather than an agent decision
evaluator agent install failures exit 1 before any spend; split/query-file validation failures stop pre-spend — harness-enforced validation mechanics
the write-back confirmation rationalization table's individual rows — one representative case (praise) is covered by writeback-confirmation; the rest are illustrative duplicates
eval agents see frontmatter-only stubs, never the skill body — harness stub design, not an agent-applied fact
eval reps run under the restricted trigger-evaluator agent installed per workspace; never default agent, never re-add --auto — harness-enforced install mechanics
manual debugging of a single query via evaluator.py run — one-line convenience detail, folded into harness-invocation practice
checklist items mirror the workflow — a compliance mirror, not reference facts
